analysis.title: Oklo - Initiate At Hold: The Future Of Fission?
key_insights: TD Cowen initiates coverage of Oklo (OKLO) at Hold with a $26 price target. The stock closed at $26.35 on 10/23/2026, so the target implies roughly no upside.
Oklo is the only public company developing a sodium fast reactor with pyroprocessing fuel recycling. TD Cowen says recycling would be disruptive if it works, but costs and execution are uncertain.
The build-own-operate model, selling power under long-term PPAs, could break the stalemate between utilities that will not take on new nuclear risk and data centers that want clean firm power.

Oklo's earlier cost estimates for reactor and fuel look extremely low. FOAK costs of $2,276/kW (15MWe) and $1,720/kW (50MWe) are below leading-edge CCGT plants at ~$3,000/kW+. Oklo has not updated them since the 2024 de-SPAC, and TD Cowen expects a cost update in 2027.

Fuel is a major risk. Oklo assumed HALEU at $7,000/kg, while current prices are ~$25,000/kg or more. That gap is ~$19/MWh undiscounted and ~$36/MWh levelized, which would materially disrupt project economics at PPA prices of ~$100-125/MWh.
Aurora's initial core is ~33% of total 40-year fuel versus 9% for the AP1000 and 13% for the Xe-100. On a 1GW basis Oklo needs ~6.6x more U3O8 than an AP1000 and ~9.5x more SWU.

A 10GW deployment would need ~1,000MT of HALEU or over 40MM SWU. Centrus plans 12MT of HALEU production into the 2030s, and current global SWU expansion plans total 18MM SWU. TD Cowen sees supply-chain bottlenecks as a meaningful risk.

Recycling spent LWR fuel costs $24,569-$56,875/kg versus fresh HALEU at $28,000/kg. Recycling spent fast-reactor fuel costs $3,902-$8,100/kg, but that feed does not exist yet. Starting with HALEU and moving to recycled fast-reactor fuel is the lowest levelized cost path.
Making LWR recycling economic would need uranium to rise from $96/lb to about $225/lb, or enrichment from $181/SWU to about $550/SWU.
Capacity factor is uncertain. Oklo's guidance assumes 92%, while EBR-II ran 70-80% and Russia's BN-600 ran in the high-70% to low-80% range.

Regulatory path: Oklo moved the INL project to the DOE pathway. The PDSA was approved on 6/11/2026, and the DSA and Readiness Review are pending. TD Cowen sees the early 2028 start-up as low probability and deployment no earlier than 2031 as the base case.
Oklo has submitted only 3 NRC topical reports, versus 17 for X-energy, 16 for TerraPower and 15 for Kairos. Its Phase 1 readiness assessment covered 1 of 24 FSAR chapters.

Customer pipeline is thin. Meta in Ohio (up to 1.2GW, first phase 2030) is the only commercial project underway. Most other agreements are non-binding MOUs from 2024 with no later updates, and the Centrus HALEU deal is only an LOI.

Capital structure: Oklo has about $3.3B of cash and securities pro forma and minimal debt. It has raised $3.0B of gross ATM proceeds at an average of $73.47 per share, including 7.26MM shares at $44.03 after 6/30. A new $1B ATM was announced 9/11/2026.

Valuation: the model assumes 10GW deployed by 2040 and 20GW by 2050, FOAK cost falling from $10K/kW to $3,250/kW, PPAs at $150/MWh, and HALEU falling from $25,000/kg to $15K and then ~$5,000/kg equivalent through recycling. The DCF uses a 14.5% WACC.
The price target is very sensitive to WACC: about $54 at 13.5% and about $315 at 10%. TD Cowen says its conviction in the target is relatively low.
Comps: Oklo's EV is $2.0B, similar to X-energy and Standard Nuclear. EV per employee is 9.8x in the comp table, and the text cites Oklo and Standard Nuclear above 20x versus ~4-5x for others.

Radioisotopes through Atomic Alchemy are a small part of the thesis. Initial revenue is expected in 1H27. BWXT sold just over 80% of its Medical business at about 40x forward EBITDA, in a deal valued at up to $800MM.

market_movers.rationale: Hold initiation with a $26 DCF-based target at a 14.5% WACC. The business model is attractive in concept, but costs, fuel supply and execution are uncertain.
Listed as an analyst top pick at $34.92 on 10/23/2026.

sector_views.rationale: Build-own-operate and fuel recycling are attractive in concept. Capital intensity, fuel cost and supply, licensing and execution risk are significant, and small input changes drive wide swings in value.

earnings_insights: Oklo FY2025A adjusted EBITDA was $(138.8)MM. TD Cowen estimates $(270.2)MM for 2026E and $(180.0)MM for 2027E, versus FactSet consensus of $(226.9)MM and $(261.1)MM.
TD Cowen revenue estimates (not reported figures) are $3.6MM for 2026E and $5.0MM for 2027E. The model has consensus revenue of about $4MM for 2026 and $15MM for 2027.

On the 2Q26 call management said it is still narrowing cost estimates with Kiewit and will provide a tighter number later. Management also said Groves could produce R&D quantities of isotopes in about 12 months, with first isotope revenue from the Idaho laboratory in 1H27.

risk_factors: Cost overruns and delays on Aurora-INL.
Higher HALEU fuel costs and constrained HALEU supply.
Weaker customer appetite for new nuclear builds.
Regulatory delays or rejections, and an untested transition from DOE authorization to NRC commercial licensing.
Capital intensity of owning and operating plants, with further equity dilution likely.
Unproven commercial-scale pyroprocessing and recycling, with a history of cost overruns in US reprocessing.
Proliferation concerns and possible public opposition to recycling.
vol_and_positioning: Oklo's 52-week range is $143.42 to $26.35, so the stock sits at the low of the range.
Oklo has raised $3B through ATM facilities in 2025 and 2026, increasing the basic share count by 27%. A new $1B ATM was announced 9/11/2026.
geopolitical: Russia is the only country to have continued commercializing sodium fast reactors, and there is currently no large-scale commercial HALEU supply outside Russia.
Proliferation concerns over plutonium from recycling and breeder reactors, including pushback from some lawmakers on the DOE Surplus Plutonium Program.

tension_points.bull_case: Recycling spent fast-reactor fuel costs $3,902-$8,100/kg versus $28,000/kg for fresh HALEU, and starting with HALEU then moving to recycled fuel is the lowest levelized cost path.
tension_points.bear_case: Recycled fast-reactor feed does not exist yet. Recycling spent LWR fuel costs $24,569-$56,875/kg, the high end above 2x HALEU, and there is no commercial pyroprocessing track record.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Uranium would need to rise from $96/lb to about $225/lb, or enrichment from $181/SWU to about $550/SWU, for LWR recycling to be economic.

tension_points.bull_case: On management's original assumptions (plant cost $2,500/kW, fuel $7,000/kg, PPA $125/MWh) a 75MW Aurora plant has an NPV of $303.8MM.
tension_points.bear_case: On market-price assumptions (plant cost $10,000/kW, fuel $25,000/kg) the same plant has an NPV of $(381.6)MM.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An updated cost disclosure for Aurora-INL, expected in 2027, would settle which case is closer.
